title: How to Take Good Pictures at Night With iPhone: Party Tips
description: How to take good pictures at night with iPhone at parties and weddings: Night mode vs flash, dark dance floors, group shots and wedding-guest etiquette.
dek: Night mode or flash, dance floors, group shots in the dark, and wedding-guest manners.
excerpt: When Night mode beats the flash, how to shoot a dark dance floor and a group in dim light, and the wedding-guest rules that keep your photos welcome.

faq.q: Is it better to use flash or Night mode at a party?
faq.a: Use Night mode when the scene is still and the room’s own light looks good, such as a candlelit table or string lights over seated guests. Use the flash for moving people, very dark rooms and dance floors, because a short burst of light freezes faces while Night mode blurs anything that moves. You can’t use both at once: turning the flash on switches Night mode off.

faq.q: Why are my iPhone photos blurry at night?
faq.a: Usually one of three things. A Night mode shot can take a second or more, so moving people or a moving hand blur; brace the phone or use the flash instead. A smudged lens spreads every light into haze; wipe it with a microfiber cloth. And zooming in dim light costs sharpness, so stay at 1x and step closer instead.

faq.q: Is it rude to take pictures at a wedding as a guest?
faq.a: Not at the reception, unless the couple has asked otherwise. The ceremony is different: if it’s unplugged, keep your phone away completely, and even when phones are allowed, skip the flash, stay seated and keep the shutter silent. Never step into the aisle or in front of the photographer, and let the couple post first before you share anything publicly.

faq.q: How do I take a good group photo in the dark?
faq.a: Move the group so everyone faces the best light in the room, stagger heights so every face is visible, and choose between flash and a very still Night mode shot. Prop the phone and use the 3, 5 or 10 second timer if you want to be in it. Take at least three frames, because the relaxed one right after the pose is usually the best.

faq.q: Should I turn off Live Photos at night?
faq.a: If you want Night mode, yes. Apple notes that turning on Live Photos or the flash switches Night mode off, so if the yellow Night mode icon never appears in a dim room, check whether Live Photos is on. If you’re using the flash anyway, Night mode is off regardless, so Live Photos makes no difference to that choice.
